title: One-step separation system of bio-functional lipid compounds from natural sources
author: Tsoupras, Pappas, et al.
materials: Furthermore, this HPLC-method has the advantage of using a semi-preparative column, and thus it can separate high amounts of dense TL-extracts into such bioactive lipid subclasses, by applying a low number of injections (1-2) in comparison to HPLC methods based in analytical grade columns where at least 10 injections are required for separating the same amount of TL-extract.

steps.title: Extract total lipids (TLs)
steps.instruction: Extract TLs from the natural source using the Bligh & Dyer method.

substeps.instruction: Homogenise the sample in a monophasic mixture of chloroform : methanol : water at a 1:2:0.8 (v/v/v) ratio.
For solid samples, blend the sample in the mixture, then filter the blend through a 110 mm Whatman filter paper under vacuum using a Buchner funnel.
Transfer the homogenate (liquid sample) or filtrate (solid sample) to a separatory funnel and add water and chloroform to adjust the overall ratio to 1:1:0.9 (v/v/v) for phase separation.
Collect the lower (chloroform) phase into a round‑bottom flask.
Evaporate the collected phase to dryness on a flash rotary evaporator set at 37 °C and 700–50 mbar vacuum.
Re‑dissolve the dried residue in chloroform : methanol 1:1 (v/v) in a small glass tube and evaporate under a stream of nitrogen.
Weigh the obtained TL, store it under nitrogen at –20 °C (maximum 8 weeks).
Immediately before HPLC analysis, dissolve the TL again in chloroform : methanol 1:1 (v/v) at room temperature.

steps.title: Set up HPLC system
steps.instruction: Prepare the HPLC instrument and column for the one‑step separation.

substeps.instruction: Install a semi‑preparative reversed‑phase Luna 5 µ C8(2) 100 Å column (Phenomenex) on an HP Series 1100 HPLC and equilibrate at 20 °C.
Use high‑purity acetonitrile (ACN) and water as mobile phases.
Set the flow rate to 3 mL/min.
Program the gradient: 0–2 min ACN : water 40:60 (v/v); 2–26 min linear gradient to 100:0 (v/v); hold 100 % ACN until 80 min (end of run).

steps.title: Prepare sample for injection
steps.instruction: Dilute the TL extract to the appropriate solvent composition for HPLC injection.

substeps.instruction: Dilute each TL sample in chloroform : methanol 1:1 (v/v).
Load the desired injection volume onto the autosampler (volume not specified in the source).

steps.title: Run HPLC separation
steps.instruction: Perform the chromatographic separation and collect lipid fractions.

substeps.instruction: Inject the diluted sample and run the programmed gradient at 3 mL/min, monitoring absorbance at 208 nm.
Collect fractions either manually according to UV peaks or automatically at fixed intervals (every 0.5 or 1 min).
Evaporate each collected fraction under a stream of nitrogen.
Re‑dissolve the dried fractions in chloroform : methanol 1:1 (v/v).
Store the re‑dissolved fractions at –20 °C for further analysis.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: Generate external or internal calibration curves for quantitative analysis of lipid subclasses.

substeps.instruction: Prepare external phospholipid (PL) stock solutions at 1 mg/mL in chloroform : methanol 1:1 (v/v) and store at –20 °C under nitrogen.
Prepare intermediate PL solutions at 20 µg/mL in the same solvent and store under the same conditions.
Serially dilute the intermediate solution to obtain a six‑point calibration curve (concentration vs. peak‑area ratio) for each PL class.
For low‑abundance molecules such as PAF, prepare an internal standard mixture of semi‑synthetic cold and ^3H‑PAF.
Quantify PAF using a calibration curve based on concentration vs. counts‑per‑minute (cpm) ratio measured with a liquid scintillation counter.
